Click a blue hex to plan a move. Turn with Q and E before you confirm. Staying in place gives enemies +10 to hit; moving 3 or more hexes normally gives them -5. Most ships can Brace instead of firing: this cuts hull damage and removes the +10, but ends the ship's turn. Glasswright ships cannot Brace.

The red ring means this enemy can be hit from where your ship sits. Click it once to see the hit chance and the damage expected. Click again to fire every gun that bears. Keys 1 to 6 fire one gun at a time.
Sides take turns, one ship at a time, until every ship has acted. That is one round. Press Space to end this ship early, or Tab for the next ship. A ship with nothing left to do ends itself.

The blue bar shows your shield pool. All four sides share it. Sides with more coverage block more damage while shields hold. Shields recharge each round. The pale bar shows hull. Hull damage needs repairs.
Press R for the threat map. It shades every hex enemy guns can reach next turn. Darker means more damage waiting there.
Reinforcements arrive at the map edge. A flash marks where they enter, and a toast names the ship. A new arrival acts in the turn order like any other ship.
Up close you have two more attacks. Press X to ram an enemy dead ahead. Press G to board an enemy next to your ship. Win a boarding and the ship is yours for the rest of the fight.

Your admiral's Command is ready. Hover over it to see what it does now and what waiting adds. You can give it once per battle. The icon turns orange after the first press; press again to give the order.
Look beside the round counter at the top left for this fight's goal. Completing that goal can win the battle even with enemy ships still on the board.

This is the sector map. Pick a stop on a connected lane and work toward the boss at the end. Stops are fights, events, rest stops, and shipyards. There is at least one elite fight on a route you can choose: harder enemies, better rewards. You cannot visit every stop, so choose.
Winning fights and some choices fill the Nemesis clock. A full clock can bring your one meeting for this sector forward. It does not add another meeting.

Winning pays credits and can offer protocols or refit modules. Sometimes you can claim a captured ship. If it would put you over your command point limit, choose Strip for salvage or Ransom for credits. A protocol reroll costs credits.
Spend credits here to repair hull damage, upgrade ships or buy new ones. Use Refits to swap modules between ships or move them to and from the hold.
The run is over, and that is expected. Losing teaches your faction: renown, core progress, and what your admiral learned all carry into the next run. Your ships and credits do not.
